prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I don’t have live access to current reviews or contractor databases, so I can’t name a single “best” company in Miami right now. I can, however, tell you exactly how to find the best contractor for a hurricane‑rated roof replacement and what to verify so you pick a reliable company.

If you want, I can also compile a short, local shortlist if you give your ZIP code — or I can draft a list of questions you can send to contractors.

What to look for when choosing a Miami roofing company for hurricane-rated replacement
- Licensing and insurance
  - Florida roofing contractor license (check on the Florida DBPR search).
  - Up‑to‑date General Liability and Workers’ Compensation insurance — ask for a certificate of insurance.
- Experience and local track record
  - Several years replacing roofs in Miami‑Dade County (HVHZ — High Velocity Hurricane Zone) with references and recent job photos.
  - Local, verifiable references you can call.
- Product and installation approvals
  - Uses materials with Miami‑Dade County Notice of Acceptance (NOA) or TAS test approvals (critical for HVHZ compliance).
  - Manufacturer certifications (e.g., GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, CertainTeed Select) — shows training and access to extended warranties.
- Building code and permitting
  - Takes care of building permits and inspections (permit pulled in owner’s name).
  - Familiar with Miami‑Dade HVHZ requirements: correct nailing/fastening, deck attachment, secondary water barrier, perimeter uplift protection, etc.
- Warranties and workmanship
  - Manufacturer’s warranty (ask exact coverage and transferability).
  - Written workmanship warranty from the contractor (duration and what’s covered).
  - Written completion and punch‑list policy.
- Contract and price clarity
  - Detailed, written contract: scope, materials (manufacturer/brand/model), fastening pattern, underlayment type, ventilation plan, start and completion dates, disposal plan, final payment terms.
  - Multiple written bids for comparison (don’t pick solely on lowest price).
- Claims and insurance help
  - Experience working with insurance claims is helpful if you’re filing; but beware contractors who pressure you to sign assignments of benefits.
- Reviews and reputation
  - Check Google, Yelp, BBB, Nextdoor, and local Facebook groups for multiple recent reviews.
  - Check for any state or local disciplinary actions.

Technical items to confirm for a hurricane‑rated replacement
- Product NOA and wind‑uplift rating (match or exceed local code; ask for the NOA number).
- Secondary water barrier (continuous, properly installed).
- Proper perimeter and corner reinforcement, approved ridge/hip assemblies.
- Fastener type and spacing per NOA/manufacturer (ring‑shank nails or screws as required).
- Adequate attic ventilation and insulation details.
- Proper flashing details (wall, chimney, skylight flashing per NOA).

Questions to ask any prospective roofer (short list)
- Are you licensed in Florida? Can you provide your license number and COI?
- Have you done hurricane‑rated roof replacements in Miami‑Dade County (HVHZ)? Can you show photos and references?
- What manufacturer and product do you recommend? Do they have an NOA for this product in Miami‑Dade?
- Will you pull permits and schedule inspections? Who is the point of contact?
- What warranties do you provide (workmanship and manufacturer)?
- How do you protect landscaping and handle cleanup and dumpster removal?
- What is your payment schedule? Do you require an assignment of benefits?

If you want, I can:
- Build a tailored shortlist of top-rated Miami roofers if you give your ZIP code, or
- Draft an email/phone script you can use to solicit bids and compare proposals.

Which would you prefer?
